findings_corrected.resolution: The sole native-open-token-and-custody-correspond oracle now owns the mutant empty post-exit file content/size as well as token reporting, follow-up refusal/native absence, affected receipts and Held cleanup. Other file checks are limited to unchanged identity/type and allowed bounds, avoiding a collateral exact-content failure.

The parent supervisor is explicitly inside the same pinned isolated Linux instance. A fresh exec child receives only reviewed allowed directory/report descriptors and immutable identity through explicit fork/exec inheritance and CLOEXEC handling. No Mac/host fd integer crosses a container command; the supervisor never invokes the attempt engine.

Every explicit child report/output descriptor is prepared before entry. No further explicit child fd acquisition follows entry. Unknown close forbids reuse of the saved custody token; it does not claim the OS or transitive runtime never reuses its numeric value.

The independent parent observer requires nofollow/CLOEXEC and opened-descriptor identity agreement before any read. All future cases use a fresh process/directory and at most one fixed file; collision owns its sentinel and no-owner has no file.
